routesElsewhere.note: On confirmation the card fields are filled from the record — name, photograph, class or role, identifier and expiry. They are not typed by hand (BR-4).

steps.note: One step. The fields are filled from the record on confirmation and are not typed (BR-4). For a pickup card they are the **child's** own photograph and details, since the guard confirms the card against the child being released rather than against the person holding it (BR-9).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A record with no photograph cannot produce a card, and a child already at the card limit gets no further one.
plan.atomicity: One write: the card, its number and the record of the issue together or not at all. The first card is free, for a student and an employee alike (BR-5). Printing happens only from the preview, singly or as a batch — there is no route that prints from anywhere else (BR-7, E6), so printing is a screen act rather than something a plan performs. **For a pickup card, nothing is recorded about who will hold it** (BR-8, E11).

operations.name: card.issue
operations.idempotencyKey: person_id + card_type, since a student or staff card is one per person; a pickup card is bounded by the limit instead
operations.purpose: Produce a card for a confirmed person, filled from their record.

parameters.name: person_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No record matches, or the person is outside the actor's scope. Withdrawn students are excluded by default, since a card must not be issued to a child who has left (BR-3, E1, E3).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, showing each candidate with their photograph, name, father's name, class and section or role, and identifier. A single mistyped digit resolves to a real record and produces a valid card carrying another child's photograph, and this confirmation is the only thing standing between the two (BR-1, BR-2).

parameters.notes: The person the card is for. A typed identifier is never silently accepted — the matched person is shown with their photograph, name, father's name, class and section or role, and identifier, and the user confirms before any field is populated (BR-2).

parameters.name: card_type
parameters.notes: What kind of card is being produced (BR-6). All three follow the same flow; what varies is the type and its source record. A pickup card names a child and is filled from the student record (BR-9).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: card_id
fields.description: The card.

fields.name: card_number
fields.description: Unique. On a pickup card it is the only thing that identifies which key was used (BR-5, BR-14).

fields.name: person
fields.description: The confirmed person — photograph, name, father's name, class and section or role, and identifier, as shown before confirmation (BR-2).

fields.name: fields_filled
fields.description: Name, photograph, class or role, identifier and expiry, all from the record (BR-4).

fields.name: expiry
fields.description: Filled from the record, not typed.

fields.name: cards_in_circulation
fields.description: For a pickup card, how many that child now has. Every one is another key to that child (BR-10).

fields.name: card_limit
fields.description: How many the School Admin permits (BR-10).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Previewed until it is printed from the preview and handed over (BR-7).

fields.name: charge
fields.description: Zero. The first card is free for a student and an employee alike (BR-5).

errors.meaning: The typed identifier matches no record.

errors.note: A card without one identifies nobody.

errors.meaning: The child is already at the pickup card limit.
errors.note: Every card in circulation is another key to that child. Void one before issuing another (BR-10).

errors.meaning: The person is a withdrawn student.
errors.note: A card must not be issued to a child who has left (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Never accept a typed identifier without the person being confirmed. A single mistyped digit resolves to a real record and produces a valid card carrying another child's photograph, and this confirmation is the only thing standing between the two (BR-2, E4).

Never fill a card field by hand. On confirmation they come from the record — name, photograph, class or role, identifier and expiry (BR-4) — and a value a planner supplied is a card that says something the record does not.

Name the person back in full before the card is produced. Photograph, name, father's name, class and section or role, and identifier: names repeat constantly, and this is the last check before a card exists (BR-1, BR-2).

Never record or ask who will hold a pickup card. It is a bearer card and the school holds no such record anywhere — there is no field for it (BR-8, E11). A plan that captured a holder's name would be inventing a record the design deliberately does not keep.

Say that a pickup card carries the child's photograph, not the holder's. The guard is confirming that the card matches the child being released (BR-9), which is what makes a bearer card checkable at all.
Report the cards now in circulation for that child against the limit. Every one is another key, and a family holding six has six ways to lose one (BR-10).
Never issue to a withdrawn student. They are excluded from the picker by default, and a card issued to a child who has left is a card that still opens a gate (BR-3, E3).
Say that printing happens from the preview. There is no route that prints from anywhere else (BR-7, E6), so the plan produces the card and a person prints it while looking at the photograph.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A card is never deleted. One issued in error is voided, and a replacement generates a new number (BR-5). A voided card is never reactivated (BR-15).

intent.name: card.replace
intent.summary: Issue a replacement card, which generates a new number and voids the old one. One step, and a voided card is never restored.
routesHere: issue a replacement — the card was damaged

routesHere.text: card kharab ho gaya hai, naya jari kar do
routesHere.gloss: the card is damaged, issue a new one

routesHere.gloss: the card has expired, make a new one

routesHere.text: gum shuda card mil gaya hai, wahi dobara chalu kar do
routesHere.gloss: the lost card has been found, reactivate it

request.text: card gum hone ki itla do
request.gloss: report the card lost

routesElsewhere.note: A card reported lost is voided immediately, before any replacement is produced (BR-11).

request.text: purana card dobara chalu kar do
request.gloss: bring the old card back into use

routesElsewhere.note: A voided card is never reactivated. A family who finds a card they reported lost is issued a replacement instead, because the school cannot know whose hands it passed through in the meantime (BR-15, E10).

steps.note: One step. The replacement generates a new number and voids the old (BR-5), so the previous card stops working the moment this one exists.

plan.atomicity: One write: the new card, its new number, and the old card voided together or not at all. A replacement for a lost card is charged and the guardian pays it for a student card (BR-5) — whether a card replaced because it expired is charged is not decided, and neither is whether a replacement pickup card is. The old card is never restored, whatever happens to it afterwards (BR-15).

operations.name: card.replace
operations.idempotencyKey: card_id, since a card is replaced once
operations.purpose: Issue a replacement card, voiding the old one.

parameters.name: card_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the cards with their number, type, the person or child they name, and their status.

parameters.notes: The issued card, resolved from the person or child it names and its number.

parameters.name: replacement_reason
parameters.type: enum: Lost | Damaged | Expired | Details changed
parameters.notes: Why a replacement is being issued (BR-5). It decides whether a charge is raised — a lost card is charged — so it is never inferred from the state of the old card.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: card_id
fields.description: The new card.

fields.name: card_number
fields.description: A new number (BR-5).

fields.name: previous_card_number
fields.description: The old one, now void and never reactivated (BR-15).

fields.name: replacement_reason
fields.description: As given.

fields.name: charge_raised
fields.description: True where the card was lost. Accounts raise the invoice, and the guardian pays it for a student card (BR-5).

fields.name: charge_undecided
fields.description: True where the reason is Expired or the card is a pickup card — whether either is charged is not decided.

fields.name: cards_in_circulation
fields.description: For a pickup card, how many that child now has. The replacement does not add to the count, since the old one is voided.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Previewed until it is printed from the preview (BR-7).

errors.meaning: A voided card was reactivated rather than replaced.
errors.note: There is no such control. The school cannot know whose hands it passed through (BR-15).

planningRules.rule: Never choose the replacement reason. It decides whether the family is charged (BR-5), and a damaged card recorded as lost puts a bill on a household that did not lose anything.

Never restore a found card. A voided card is never reactivated and a replacement is issued instead (BR-15, E10) — the school cannot know whose hands it passed through while it was lost, and with a bearer card that is the whole risk.

Report the charge, and say where it is undecided. A lost card is charged; whether an expired one is, and whether a replacement pickup card is, are both open — and the use case notes that charging for a lost pickup card may discourage the report the school most needs.
Report that the previous card is void. It stops working the moment the replacement exists (BR-5), which matters most on a pickup card somebody may still be carrying.
Never replace a lost card without the loss being reported first. The void comes first, then the replacement (BR-11).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A replacement is not undone. The old card stays void and the new one stands (BR-5, BR-15).

Say plainly that whoever presents the card may collect the child. A guardian handing one to a driver is handing over a key, and the notification on issue says so for the same reason.
Never request several children in one call. Each child's cards are counted against their own limit (BR-10).

operations.name: pickup.card.void

operations.purpose: Void one pickup card, effective immediately.

parameters.name: card_id

parameters.notes: The card being voided. On a pickup card the number is the only thing that identifies which key it is (BR-14).

parameters.name: void_reason
parameters.type: enum: Reported lost | Not returned | Child withdrawn | Replaced | Withdrawn by the school
parameters.notes: Why it is being voided (BR-11). Reporting one lost is the commonest. The reason distinguishes a card the family lost from one the school stopped, which is what the voided-cards report is read for.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: card_id

fields.name: card_number
fields.description: The number now void — the only identifier a bearer card has (BR-14).

fields.name: void_reason
fields.description: As given.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Voided. It fails at the gate at once (BR-11, E9).

fields.description: How many cards that child still has in circulation (BR-10).

fields.name: guardian_notified
fields.description: Delivery status.

fields.name: gate_notified
fields.description: Repeated until acknowledged at the gate, because a voided card that the gate has not heard about is still a working key.

errors.meaning: The card is already voided or replaced.

planningRules.rule: Never defer a void. It fails at the gate within seconds, not at the end of the day, and until it is voided whoever holds it can collect the child (BR-11).
Never choose the void reason. Reported lost, not returned and withdrawn by the school are different facts, and the voided-cards report is read to tell them apart (BR-11).
Report how many cards that child still has. Voiding one leaves the others working, and a family who thinks they have stopped collection has not (BR-10).
Report the gate notification separately. A voided card the gate has not acknowledged is still a working key in practice, which is why that message repeats until it is.
Never treat a void as reversible. A voided card is never reactivated, and a found card is replaced rather than restored (BR-15, E10).
